name: memory_recall
title: Recall memories
description: Search persistent memory for facts a past session saved. Call it BEFORE starting a task that resembles past work, and when the user refers to something decided earlier; use memory_save to add a fact, and memory_compact or memory_dream only to tidy the store — this tool never changes what a fact says. Reads every layer in order — the project store, any read-only grants in .bantamkit/config.yaml, then the machine-wide profile — and returns the top word matches, never fewer than the store default of 3 when that many match; a query that is exactly a fact's name returns that fact alone. Pass `file` instead of `query` to see the facts linked to a file. Why it is not read-only: every hit is appended to the usage ledger (~/.bantamkit/usage/<store-id>.jsonl) as a recall event — the staleness order memory_compact archives by — and a project fact file still in the 0.35.x format is rewritten once into the current one; both are best-effort and never fail a recall. A fact file that cannot be read is named in the reply, never silently skipped.

query.description: Words a past-you would have used to describe the fact

k.description: Facts wanted, clamped to 1..5. Raised to the store default of 3 when smaller; never lowered below it.

include_archived.description: Also search facts compaction moved to archive/. Archived matches come after the live ones, tagged [archived].

file.description: A tracked file, or the shortest unique suffix of one (store.ts, memory/store.ts). Returns the facts linked to it and when it was last touched; query is then ignored.
